questions.text: In the describe → decide → execute → observe loop, what happens after the model emits a structured tool call?

options.A: The model runs the executor and updates external state directly.
options.B: The host validates arguments, runs the executor, and returns its result to the model.
options.C: The host treats the call arguments as the completed tool result.
options.D: The model treats the tool description as evidence that the action succeeded.

questions.explanation: A tool call requests an action. The host validates and executes it, then supplies the result so the model can observe it.

questions.text: Two independent tool calls finish in the reverse order from which they were requested. How should the host associate each result with its request?

options.A: Match each result to the earliest request without a result.
options.B: Match each result using only the tool name.
options.C: Match each result using its corresponding call ID.
options.D: Match each result using its position in the completion list.

questions.explanation: Call IDs correlate results with specific requests even when execution finishes out of order or the same tool is called twice.

questions.text: In run_loop, a selected tool has consequential=True. The code prints "GATE : tool is consequential, would confirm" and then calls tool.executor. What does this actually enforce?

options.A: It reports the classification but still executes without obtaining confirmation.
options.B: It pauses execution until the user explicitly approves the call.
options.C: It rejects consequential tools before their executors can run.
options.D: It runs the executor only against a read-only copy of external state.

questions.explanation: Printing a gate message does not enforce approval. This implementation proceeds directly to tool.executor.
